what: GitLab is a software development platform: source code management, automated testing and deployment, security scanning and project planning, all in one application rather than a stack of separate tools.
customers: Software engineering organisations, from startups to large enterprises, on per-seat subscriptions.
money: seats on the platform, hosted or on the customer's own servers
moat: Source code repositories and the automated pipelines built around them, which is where a company's entire engineering workflow lives. Moving it is a months-long project.
risks: A $53M net loss, mostly stock compensation
GitHub has far more users and is bundled with Microsoft's enterprise agreements
AI coding tools could reduce the number of developer seats companies buy
opportunities: $214M of free cash flow and $230M of cash with no debt
Revenue grew from $253M to $955M in four years
Analysts see about 29% upside, with 24 covering the stock, and its higher tiers sell security and compliance features
watch: Net dollar retention and the number of customers paying over $100,000 a year.
